name: Craftweld Fabrication Co Inc
old_description: Commercial blade protectors are required to move any bulldozer with a blade greater than 10 feet and no greater than 15 feet. We have been providing commercial bulldozer blades to the public since 1987. We provide a serial number with each purchase and the option to transfer serial numbers. Please visit our page on Blade Protectors to view the laws and literature pertaining to moving commercial equipment.
about:
Craftweld Fabrication Co. Inc. operates from Montgomeryville, Pennsylvania, where it was founded in 1987. The company began by supplying commercial blade protectors required for transporting bulldozers with blades between 10 and 15 feet, providing serial-numbered units with transferable registration. Over the past three decades it has expanded into a full-service fabrication and machining shop serving a range of industrial sectors.

The shop combines design, fabrication, and machining under one roof. Its engineering team uses Autodesk Inventor for 3D CAD modeling and drawing packages, while the production floor runs CNC turning, milling, and sawing alongside manual counterparts. Metal forming is handled by four Accurpress hydraulic press brakes (80 to 500 tons, up to 14-foot capacity), a Whitney 30-ton CNC programmable press punch, and an Autosert hardware insertion press. Two Bystronic CO2 lasers (ByVention and Bystar) provide laser cutting. The facility also supports welding, finishing, and assembly of sub-assemblies, process skids, carts, cabinets, and plastic components.

Craftweld’s original customer base centered on contractors and equipment movers needing compliant blade protectors for bulldozers. Today the company works with clients across multiple industries that require custom metal fabrications, stainless-steel assemblies, structural components, and machinery parts. The staff assists with troubleshooting, material selection, and manufacturing technique decisions to turn customer designs into finished products.

The company emphasizes a blend of current technology and traditional design knowledge, maintaining what it describes as a personal family atmosphere and close customer relationships. Its stated differentiation lies in offering design-for-manufacturability support, rapid quoting on laser work regardless of quantity, and a single-source capability from CAD models through finished fabrication.
